lane: hostregime-sm (perf-hostregime-statemachine2-fast, successor; probe-only; series launched by perf-hostregime-statemachine-fast which died in the machine death ~07:51-08:18Z)
hypothesis: The write-regime state machine (20260929-223000) separated three classes - the per-host fast/slow machine (flips ~7-8min), the fleet incident phase (shared sandbox-storage backend, all-VM onset +/-8s, repeat-fsync LIFTED 12-16x), and the working-VM deep band (~19% wall time, repeat-fsync flat) - but through 2026-10-01 early hours every working bench VM sat in a fresh-create deep class the census had never sampled on idle hosts (redecompose 43.7ms iso p50 for a whole session, probe-grid 115-136ms at boundaries, createwall 245ms crossings, kernel-async 72-74ms fresh p50): the state set, its switching scales, and its CURRENT occupancy are uncharacterized on the hosts lanes actually use - the gate-pool VMs (aged, 67-136 gate runs) and the fresh bench class - leaving lanes unable to distinguish a host state from a fleet phase from a product effect at their next boundary. Census questions: what is the state set per host class NOW (fast ~1 / slow ~2.5 / the new fresh-create deep class); the dwell/switching rates; the class structure of each state (which probe classes lift); the cross-host (de)synchronization and the fleet-incident signature lanes should recognize; the CURRENT regime census every lane can cite.
approach: 8 hosts, the standing instrument (probe_regime.py, the write-regime/hoststat census instrument +statvfs), flock-guarded single instance, duration 9000s, pre-registered analysis in DESIGN.md (written before analysis): (1) 3 fresh bench-class VMs hr-a/b/c (16c/32GB/40GB ubuntu:22.04, the hoststat census class - python3 apt-installed, launch window labeled NON-AMBIENT, the hoststat precedent); (2) ALL 4 gate-pool VMs (fleet-gate-pool-0/1/2/3, rust:1-bookworm 8c/32GB/100GB, aged 1-136 gate runs; pool-0 joined 20min late after its gate slot freed; slots watched for gate claims - gate-load windows labeled, never dropped); (3) the orchestrator-box control orch (60s cadence, no dense stream - the write-regime lane's LOCAL-BOX control: the shared-backend phases leave it untouched). Every dense host: DENSE 0.5s ISOLATED fresh4k+sync_all+rename (advisory v1.0 class 1, continuous) + 30s rich dual-class samples (fresh4k/64k/256k+sync_all+rename, fresh4k+fdatasync+rename, fresh4k nofsync-rename control, append+fsync, repeat-fsync 4KB class 2, cached-read, O_DIRECT controls) + per-sample host counters (PSI io/cpu/mem, meminfo Dirty/Writeback, vmstat, diskstats, cgroup io.stat, loadavg, statvfs). NO burst tests (self-induction settled by the source record; ambient census only). Analyzer: 30s windows; window baseline = median non-stall (<=15ms) ops, all-ops-stall windows take med_all + deep flag (NO-CEILING, never blended); bands = 1-D k-means in log space, centroids >=1.6x apart, >=4% occupancy; validated BEFORE analysis on the write-regime 6h raw series (reproduces its bands, ~7-8min flip rates, and the 1799.7/2254.7ms phase-max pair exactly) and on the hoststat raw series (reproduces 0.89/2.4-2.5 bands, 4.4-6.8/h transitions, 8.4/h traps).
parity_notes: Infra lane, record only: NO product code changed, no product build measured; frozen parity surfaces untouched by construction. All claims are about host/storage infrastructure.

key_findings:
THE HOST-REGIME STATE MACHINE IS PER-HOST-CLASS AND NOW FULLY CENSUSED (7 hosts x 2.5h, dense 0.5s ISOLATED fresh4k+sync_all+rename + 30s rich dual-class samples, zero gate claims in window):
(1) FRESH BENCH CLASS (hr-a/b/c): {fast ~0.84-0.90ms, slow ~2.04-2.10ms} two-state machine, flips 3.2-5.3/h per direction (steady-window 3.6-5.6/h), slow dwell med 150-180s (max 16.5-20min), fast dwell med 2.5-6.75min; slow level moved DOWN from the Sep-27 census's 2.407-2.467 to 2.04-2.10 (fast level unchanged 0.84-0.90 vs 0.878-0.889). Partial synchrony is REAL: all-three-slow 44/295 windows (14.9%) vs 3.4% under independence (4.4x enrichment) while onsets are NOT lock-step (3-9/19-25 flips within 1 window) - co-occupancy-coupled, onset-independent (distinct from the fleet incident phase's +/-8s onset). The 32-min launch transient was slow-dominant (84.5-87.9% of windows) - fresh-VM launch settling extends ~30min beyond the 3-min pre-registered exclusion (disclosed; steady occupancy fast 0.79-0.85).
(2) GATE-POOL CLASS IS PER-HOST DIVERGENT: pool-1 (136 gate runs, 90.3% disk full) sat FAST 0.703ms for the entire 2.5h - single band, ZERO transitions, psi_io ~0.0%; pool-2/pool-3 live in a FAST<->DEEP machine.
(3) THE DEEP STATE IS A PER-HOST QUANTIZED FRESH-CREATE STATE (the T+20min finding, confirmed on the full series): pool-2 DEEP = 233ms (mode cluster 230-240ms), pool-3 = 269ms (cluster 260-280ms) - DIFFERENT quanta on adjacent pool hosts; occupancy 58.3%/48.1%, episode dwell med 180s/360s, max 38.5/18.5min, flips 2.4-4.5/h; both hosts started DEEP, closed FAST; a slow-scale drift: DEEP-dominant 07:30-08:50, regime change ~08:50-09:00, fast-dominant after.
(4) CLASS STRUCTURE (rule-B): the DEEP state lifts ONLY fresh-small-file+fsync classes - fresh4k 0.696->232.6 / fresh64k 0.724->232.3 / fdatasync 0.618->231.5 (pool-2; pool-3 identical shape at 267-268) - while fresh256k 1.08/1.38 STAYS FAST (the sharp size discriminator), append 0.479/0.469, repeat-fsync 0.405/0.394, nofsync 0.048/0.053, cached 0.016/0.017, O_DIRECT 0.128/0.137 ALL FLAT => HOST STATE, not a fleet phase (repeat-fsync never lifted anywhere; hr slow state shows the SAME signature at 2.4x scale: fresh4k 0.75-0.79->1.79-1.91, 64k 0.79-0.84->1.76-1.82 lifted; repeat 0.51-0.57->0.51-0.54, append, fresh256k, nofsync FLAT).
(5) THE DEEP STATE IS EXTERNAL HOST-LOCAL PRESSURE: psi_io some avg60 med 33.8%/36.5% in DEEP vs 1.4%/1.9% fast (pool-1 0.0% all window), while the probe's OWN cg write rate is ~0.0-0.1MB/s in BOTH states, Dirty med 0.06-0.09MB, Writeback 0, in_flight 0 in BOTH => the VM's own writeback is idle; the pressure is on the shared device from OUTSIDE the VM. The hr slow state shows psi ~0.02-0.07% in BOTH states => NOT pressure-correlated (internal host state).
(6) FLEET COUPLING: NO fleet incident phase this window. pool-2~pool-3 both-DEEP 100/295 vs 83 if independent (1.2x - long episodes overlap on a shared pressure baseline) but DEEP onsets do NOT match (0/6 within 1 window) => per-host independent switching. Cross-class matched traps ~0 (hr~pool all 0). The ORCH-DIRECTIVE question is answered: the idle-pool DEEP state (233-269ms) EXCEEDS the working-VM 40-136ms fresh-trap bands the early-hours records saw, and the two are DIFFERENT CLASSES: the fresh bench class in this census shows NO sustained DEEP state at all (0.3-0.7% of windows as isolated 30-60s flashes; isolated traps 0-0.8/h to 656-868ms) - working-VM 40-136ms bands were that class's TRAP-INCIDENCE class, not the pool DEEP state; the DEEP state is a gate-pool-host property with per-host quanta.
(7) TRAP CENSUS: fresh class st15 0.35-0.55%, st50 0.04-0.05%, st100 0.00-0.01%; pool-1 st15 0.55% with isolated 1040ms max (1.2/h); pool-2 st15 48.11% / st100 47.98% and pool-3 37.38%/37.10% - the DEEP state's own ops (NO-CEILING: they ARE the state, labeled, never blended).
(8) ORCH CONTROL (51min, truncated): whole flush path ~1.8-3.2ms INCLUDING repeat-fsync 1.777 - the busy-shared-box signature (uniform lift, not a state); no fleet phase occurred to re-test the LOCAL-BOX separation end-to-end.
